# hooks

```go
import "github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/runtime/v2/hooks"
```

Package hooks provides synchronous interception points for provider calls, tool execution, and session lifecycle in the PromptKit runtime.

## Constants

<a name="HookTypeProvider"></a>Hook type names as used in execconfig.ExecHook.Hook.

```go
const (
    HookTypeProvider = "provider"
    HookTypeTool     = "tool"
    HookTypeSession  = "session"
    HookTypeEval     = "eval"
)
```

<a name="DirectionInput"></a>Guardrail directions: which side of a provider call a check gates, and the vocabulary a firing is tagged with.

Both the guardrail adapter and the pipeline stage use these labels, so they live here rather than in hooks/guardrails.

```go
const (
    // DirectionInput gates the user's input, in BeforeCall.
    DirectionInput = "input"
    // DirectionOutput gates the assistant's response, in AfterCall.
    DirectionOutput = "output"
    // DirectionBoth gates input and output.
    DirectionBoth = "both"
)
```

<a name="MetadataKeyValidatorDeclaration"></a>MetadataKeyValidatorDeclaration is the Decision.Metadata key under which a pack\-declared guardrail reports its \*packspec.Validator, so the stage can put it on the validation event. The stage removes it before recording the decision on the message.

```go
const MetadataKeyValidatorDeclaration = "validator_declaration"
```

<a name="BuildExecHooks"></a>
## func [BuildExecHooks](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/exec_build.go#L50-L51>)

```go
func BuildExecHooks(bindings map[string]*execconfig.ExecHook, sandboxes map[string]sandbox.Sandbox) (provider []ProviderHook, tool []ToolHook, session []SessionHook, err error)
```

BuildExecHooks converts runtime\-config exec\-hook bindings into provider, tool, and session hook instances, resolving each binding's named sandbox from the provided map. Bindings with Hook=="eval" are skipped: eval hooks live in the evals package and are wired by the caller. This is the single source of truth for turning execconfig.ExecHook bindings into runtime hooks, used by both the SDK and Arena so the two never drift.

<a name="ResolveSandboxes"></a>
## func [ResolveSandboxes](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/exec_build.go#L22>)

```go
func ResolveSandboxes(specs map[string]*execconfig.SandboxConfig) (map[string]sandbox.Sandbox, error)
```

ResolveSandboxes builds a map from declared sandbox names to ready Sandbox instances using the process\-wide factory registry. Factories must have been registered \(via sandbox.RegisterFactory or a backend's init\) beforehand. Shared by the SDK and Arena so both resolve sandboxes identically.

<a name="BlockMessager"></a>
## type [BlockMessager](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/registry.go#L99-L101>)

BlockMessager is an optional ProviderHook interface for a hook that knows, before it fires, the messages it replaces a blocked turn with. A voice pipeline renders them as speech at session start, so the caller hears one without waiting.

```go
type BlockMessager interface {
    BlockMessages() []string
}
```

<a name="ChunkInterceptor"></a>
## type [ChunkInterceptor](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/hooks.go#L19-L21>)

ChunkInterceptor is an opt\-in streaming extension for ProviderHook. ProviderHooks that also implement ChunkInterceptor will have OnChunk called for each streaming chunk, enabling early abort.

```go
type ChunkInterceptor interface {
    OnChunk(ctx context.Context, chunk *providers.StreamChunk) Decision
}
```

<a name="ChunkRequest"></a>
## type [ChunkRequest](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/types.go#L103-L113>)

ChunkRequest is a streamed response chunk handed to a ChunkRequestInterceptor, with who the call acts for.

```go
type ChunkRequest struct {
    // Chunk is the chunk being judged. An interceptor that returns Enforced
    // rewrites Chunk.Content in place, as OnChunk does.
    Chunk *providers.StreamChunk

    // Caller is who the conversation acts for, as the host set it with
    // sdk.WithCaller. The zero value means none was set. PromptKit hands it to
    // the host's interceptor and otherwise never reads, persists, logs or
    // emits it.
    Caller types.Caller
}
```

<a name="ChunkRequestInterceptor"></a>
## type [ChunkRequestInterceptor](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/hooks.go#L27-L29>)

ChunkRequestInterceptor is ChunkInterceptor with the caller: a ProviderHook that implements it has InterceptChunk called for each streaming chunk, in place of OnChunk when it implements both, so a per\-tenant output check sees who the turn acts for.

```go
type ChunkRequestInterceptor interface {
    InterceptChunk(ctx context.Context, req ChunkRequest) Decision
}
```

<a name="Decision"></a>
## type [Decision](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/types.go#L12-L29>)

Decision is the result of a hook evaluation.

```go
type Decision struct {
    Allow    bool
    Reason   string
    Metadata map[string]any
    // Enforced indicates the hook already applied enforcement (e.g., truncated
    // or replaced content on the response). When true, the provider stage
    // records the validation result but continues the pipeline instead of
    // returning an error.
    Enforced bool

    // Hold is set by a chunk interceptor that allows a chunk: how many bytes
    // at the end of the chunk's Content it has not cleared yet, because they
    // could be the start of content it blocks once more of the reply arrives
    // (a banned word split across chunks). The provider stage keeps those
    // bytes from the caller until a later chunk clears them, completes what it
    // blocks, or the reply ends. Zero holds nothing back.
    Hold int
}
```

<a name="EmitterAware"></a>
## type [EmitterAware](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/registry.go#L30-L32>)

EmitterAware is implemented by hooks that report their own events. A hook cannot build an emitter for itself: the session and conversation IDs the events must carry are only known once the conversation exists, long after hooks are compiled from the pack.

The provider stage constructor holds both the emitter and the hook registry, so it joins the two.

```go
type EmitterAware interface {
    SetEmitter(*events.Emitter)
}
```

<a name="ExecHookConfig"></a>
## type [ExecHookConfig](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/exec_hooks.go#L31-L40>)

ExecHookConfig holds the configuration for creating exec\-based hooks.

Sandbox, when non\-nil, controls how the hook subprocess is launched. When nil, the exec hooks use the built\-in direct sandbox, which runs exec.CommandContext\(Command, Args...\) in\-process with the local environment. SDK consumers that want their hooks to run elsewhere \(in a sidecar, a disposable container, a managed cloud sandbox\) construct a Sandbox implementation and pass it here.

The hook's stdin is the JSON of the request or event it handles, the conversation's caller \(types.Caller, under "Caller"\) included: an exec hook is host policy code run out of process, so it gets the caller as an in\-process hook does. A Sandbox that runs the hook remotely carries the caller there.

```go
type ExecHookConfig struct {
    Name      string
    Command   string
    Args      []string
    Env       []string
    TimeoutMs int
    Phases    []string
    Mode      string // "filter" | "observe"
    Sandbox   sandbox.Sandbox
}
```

<a name="InputRequest"></a>
## type [InputRequest](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/types.go#L126-L139>)

InputRequest is the narrow view of an about\-to\-be\-sent call handed to a func\-based input guardrail. Use guardrails.InputFunc to build one.

```go
type InputRequest struct {
    // UserInput is the text of the user message being gated.
    UserInput string
    // Messages is the full conversation history including that message.
    Messages []types.Message
    // Round is the provider round this call belongs to (1-based).
    Round int
    // Replacement supplies the canned assistant text when the check
    // returns Enforced. Empty falls back to the default blocked message.
    Replacement string
    // Caller is who the conversation acts for, as the host set it with
    // sdk.WithCaller. The zero value means none was set.
    Caller types.Caller
}
```

<a name="ProviderRequest"></a>
## type [ProviderRequest](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/types.go#L65-L99>)

ProviderRequest describes an LLM call about to be made.

```go
type ProviderRequest struct {
    ProviderID   string
    Model        string
    Messages     []types.Message
    SystemPrompt string
    Round        int
    Metadata     map[string]any

    // TurnIndex is the 0-based turn this call belongs to: 0 for the
    // conversation's first turn, on the text path (Send, Stream) and the
    // realtime path alike, counted from the persisted transcript. A text
    // pipeline built without a state store (sdk.Open always has one) has no
    // transcript to count, and reports 0 on every turn. Round is not a substitute: it counts tool-loop
    // rounds within one turn and restarts in each composition sub-pipeline.
    TurnIndex int

    // Prompt is the pack's definition of the prompt the model is being
    // invoked for, a read-only copy taken when the conversation was built.
    // After a workflow handoff it is the destination state's prompt. Nil means
    // undeclared. PromptKit never reads it.
    Prompt *packspec.Prompt

    // Replacement is written by a BeforeCall hook that returns Enforced, to
    // supply the assistant text returned in place of the blocked provider
    // call. Mirrors how output guardrails mutate resp.Message in AfterCall.
    // Empty falls back to Decision.Metadata["replacement"], then to
    // prompt.DefaultBlockedMessage.
    Replacement string

    // Caller is who the conversation acts for, as the host set it with
    // sdk.WithCaller. The zero value means none was set. PromptKit hands it to
    // the host's provider hooks, guardrails included, and otherwise never
    // reads, persists, logs or emits it.
    Caller types.Caller
}
```

<a name="Registry.RunBeforeProviderCall"></a>
### func \(\*Registry\) [RunBeforeProviderCall](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/registry.go#L159>)

```go
func (r *Registry) RunBeforeProviderCall(ctx context.Context, req *ProviderRequest) Decision
```

RunBeforeProviderCall executes all provider hooks' BeforeCall in order. The first non\-Allow decision wins and short\-circuits.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

ExampleRegistry\_RunBeforeProviderCall shows registering a ProviderHook and running it before an LLM call. Hooks run in registration order; the first denial short\-circuits the chain and its Decision is returned.

```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/runtime/v2/hooks"
)

// modelDenylist is a minimal hooks.ProviderHook that blocks calls to a
// specific model. Real hooks (e.g. runtime/hooks/guardrails) do content
// moderation, PII redaction, and similar — this shows the shape any
// ProviderHook implementation takes.
type modelDenylist struct {
	banned string
}

func (d modelDenylist) Name() string { return "model-denylist" }

func (d modelDenylist) BeforeCall(_ context.Context, req *hooks.ProviderRequest) hooks.Decision {
	if req.Model == d.banned {
		return hooks.Deny("model is not allowed")
	}
	return hooks.Allow
}

func (d modelDenylist) AfterCall(_ context.Context, _ *hooks.ProviderRequest, _ *hooks.ProviderResponse) hooks.Decision {
	return hooks.Allow
}

// ExampleRegistry_RunBeforeProviderCall shows registering a ProviderHook and
// running it before an LLM call. Hooks run in registration order; the first
// denial short-circuits the chain and its Decision is returned.
func main() {
	reg := hooks.NewRegistry(hooks.WithProviderHook(modelDenylist{banned: "banned-model"}))

	decision := reg.RunBeforeProviderCall(context.Background(), &hooks.ProviderRequest{Model: "banned-model"})
	fmt.Println(decision.Allow, decision.Reason)
}
```

#### Output

```
false model is not allowed
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Registry.RunOnChunkRequest"></a>
### func \(\*Registry\) [RunOnChunkRequest](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/registry.go#L228>)

```go
func (r *Registry) RunOnChunkRequest(ctx context.Context, req ChunkRequest) Decision
```

RunOnChunkRequest executes all chunk interceptors in order: InterceptChunk for one that implements ChunkRequestInterceptor, OnChunk otherwise. First deny wins and short\-circuits. When every interceptor allows the chunk, the decision holds back the most any of them holds \(Decision.Hold\).

<a name="SessionEvent"></a>
## type [SessionEvent](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/types.go#L190-L202>)

SessionEvent carries context for session lifecycle hooks.

```go
type SessionEvent struct {
    SessionID      string
    ConversationID string
    Messages       []types.Message
    TurnIndex      int
    Metadata       map[string]any

    // Caller is who the conversation acts for, as the host set it with
    // sdk.WithCaller. The zero value means none was set. PromptKit hands it to
    // the host's session hooks, an exec hook included (as "Caller" in its stdin
    // JSON), and otherwise never reads, persists, logs or emits it.
    Caller types.Caller
}
```

<a name="ToolRequest"></a>
## type [ToolRequest](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/types.go#L162-L178>)

ToolRequest describes a tool call about to be executed.

```go
type ToolRequest struct {
    Name   string
    Args   json.RawMessage
    CallID string

    // Declaration is the pack's definition of the tool, the same value its
    // executor receives on tools.ToolDescriptor.Declaration, so a host that
    // only allows or denies needs one hook covering every tool. Nil means the
    // pack does not declare the tool. PromptKit never reads it.
    Declaration *packspec.Tool

    // Caller is who the conversation acts for, as the host set it with
    // sdk.WithCaller. The zero value means none was set. PromptKit hands it to
    // the host's tool hooks, an exec hook included (as "Caller" in its stdin
    // JSON), and otherwise never reads, persists, logs or emits it.
    Caller types.Caller
}
```

<a name="ToolResultRewriter"></a>
## type [ToolResultRewriter](<https://github.com/AltairaLabs/PromptKit/blob/main/runtime/hooks/hooks.go#L56-L58>)

ToolResultRewriter is an opt\-in extension for ToolHook. A ToolHook that also implements it may rewrite the text of a tool's successful result before the model sees it, as a test harness does to plant an indirect prompt injection in live tool output.

The provider stage calls it for the tools it runs: once with a plain result's text, or once per text part of a multimodal result, before the result size limit applies, on text turns and realtime duplex sessions alike. Rewriters run in registration order, each on the previous one's output; an error fails the tool call. The SDK also runs it on the results a host settles outside the turn and delivers with Continue, ContinueDuplex or Resume \(an approved call, a client tool's answer\), with the request the stage would give for the call \(an approval with edits gives the edited arguments\), and the history keeps the rewritten result. On Resume it runs on the client's answer as sent, which is not formatted or truncated, and what is replayed from the history \(to AG\-UI, say\) is the rewritten text. Parallel tool calls rewrite concurrently, so RewriteResult must be safe for concurrent use.

```go
type ToolResultRewriter interface {
    RewriteResult(ctx context.Context, req ToolRequest, content string) (string, error)
}
```
